entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: EMA recommends authorisation of Rasonque for metastatic pancreatic cancer
entries.description: EMA’s human medicines committee (CHMP) has recommended granting a marketing authorisation in the European Union for Rasonque (daraxonrasib), an oral treatment for adults with…
entries.summary: EMA’s CHMP has recommended approval of Rasonque for metastatic pancreatic cancer.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must prepare for market authorization and adjust regulatory submissions for this oral small molecule in the EU.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Health Canada launches pilot for select academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials: Notice
entries.description: Health Canada launches a pilot for select academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials.  If the criteria for the pilot are met and the trial is accepted under the pilot, sponsors will not be expected to comply with all of the regulatory requirements.
entries.summary: Health Canada has launched a pilot program for selected academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials that, if accepted, exempts sponsors from some regulatory requirements.
entries.why_it_matters: Academic sponsors and RA teams working on pediatric studies must monitor eligibility criteria and understand the reduced regulatory obligations under the pilot.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register listing drugs that meet the criteria of sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations has been established.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor this register to ensure that any applicable innovative drugs are identified and tracked for compliance purposes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Qualifying notice for Hernexeos (304237)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada authorized Hernexeos under a Notice of Compliance with Conditions, requiring the sponsor to conduct additional studies to verify clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams must plan, monitor, and ensure completion of the additional studies to satisfy the condition and maintain market authorization.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA provides clarifications on the Paediatric Investigation Plan (PIP) compliance verification procedure and paediatric rewards.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for paediatric studies must review the clarified verification steps to ensure compliance and timely access to paediatric incentives.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: This update provides compressed ASCII text files containing the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams can use these files to review and analyze NOC information for compliance tracking.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot will become a permanent initiative effective January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams preparing clinical trial applications must now plan to use the ACT EU guidance as an ongoing resource, affecting all sponsors and submission planning.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety updates have been applied to product monographs for submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must update their documentation to reflect the new brand safety criteria, affecting all product monograph submissions within the specified period.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Guide clarifies reporting requirements for drug shortages and discontinuations under sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Market authorization holders must report drug shortages and discontinuations, so RA teams need to incorporate these reporting steps into their processes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance on complying with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 for distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must ensure their distribution plans align with the specified regulations when exporting Canadian‑marketed drugs, affecting all establishment licence holders.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: This guide explains how drug establishment licence holders can import and sell drugs to address shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must follow sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations to ensure compliant supply during shortages.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: This guide explains how to extend expiration dates of marketed drugs to address shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must ensure compliance with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations when adjusting expiry dates to manage shortages.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: The EMA issued procedural advice on pre‑authorisation for applicants using the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams handling centralised applications must review the updated procedural guidance to ensure compliance with the latest EMA expectations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: A data extract of the Drug Product Database (DPD) has been released, providing complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams can now access comprehensive DPD data to support product submissions and compliance activities.

entries.title: List of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to the product information
entries.description: List of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to the product information
entries.summary: The document lists centrally authorised products whose safety information has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review these changes to ensure product information is current and compliant with regulatory requirements.

entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026
entries.description: Marketing authorisation holders wishing to receive an outcome in 2026 should submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings…
entries.summary: Advice on end‑of‑year submission dates for type I variations in 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Marketing authorisation holders need to plan to submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super‑groupings before the 2026 deadline.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…
entries.summary: EMA has endorsed a joint statement urging the advancement of alternatives to animal testing throughout the medicine lifecycle.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams across all therapeutic areas should anticipate shifts toward non‑animal testing methods and prepare to align submissions and quality systems accordingly.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams should note the upcoming policy shift, as it will affect the development and regulatory strategy for products in women’s health.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Women are missing from medicines development: EMA’s roadmap for change
entries.description: By the end of 2026, EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap to help drive decisive change on how women’s health is considered across medicines development and regulation. This…,         Women are still missing: from research and data, prevention, diagnosis and treatment. But the momentum to improve support for women’s health has never been stronger.…,         Meaningful change starts with dialogue and with a shared understanding of the challenges we face. We end this workshop with a clear path to action”, “National regulatory…,   The multistakeholder workshop, broadcast live, brought together over 100 leading voices on women’s health at EU and international level, from regulators to patients, healthcare…
entries.summary: EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap by the end of 2026 to address the lack of women’s representation in medicines development.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must consider how to incorporate women-specific data and requirements into their development plans and regulatory submissions.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Updated Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications
entries.description: Listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.summary: Updated list of drugs eligible for supplementary protection certificates
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review their product portfolios to ensure compliance with supplementary protection certificate regulations

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.description: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.summary: Member states have designated contact points to review the national implementation of QR codes for veterinary medicinal products authorised through centralised, mutual recognition, decentralised and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams in veterinary pharmaceutical companies need to be aware of these contact points to ensure compliance with QR code requirements and to facilitate communication during national reviews.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: INS-GCP-1 procedure for coordinating good-clinical-practice inspections requested by the CHMP
entries.description: INS-GCP-1 procedure for coordinating good-clinical-practice inspections requested by the CHMP
entries.summary: A new procedure INS‑GCP‑1 has been established for coordinating good‑clinical‑practice inspections requested by the CHMP.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams involved in clinical trials must adopt this procedure to ensure timely coordination of GCP inspections and compliance with CHMP requests.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list
entries.description: This is a list of certain generic drug submissions currently under review. The Generic Submissions Under Review list includes the medicinal ingredient(s) and therapeutic area. Downloadable Excel files are included.
entries.summary: Monthly update released to the Generic Submissions Under Review list.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should note the updated status of generic drug submissions and review the list to stay informed of current review positions.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.description: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.summary: Certain substances are excluded from the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 for residues of veterinary medicinal products in animal foodstuffs.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware that these substances are not subject to the regulation, affecting residue monitoring and compliance requirements for veterinary products.

entries.summary: MHRA launched a new Regulatory Advice Service for medical devices in December 2025.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams developing medical devices can now meet directly with MHRA to clarify requirements, impacting their regulatory strategy and compliance planning.

entries.description: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.summary: New pharmacovigilance recommendations are issued for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products in 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams working on veterinary products must update their pharmacovigilance plans to align with the new recommendations.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines

entries.description: Draft guideline on veterinary good pharmacovigilance practices (VGVP) Module: Signal Management - Revision 1
entries.summary: Revision 1 of the draft guideline on veterinary good pharmacovigilance practices introduces updated signal management procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: Veterinary RA teams must review the new signal management framework to align their pharmacovigilance processes and reporting requirements.
